newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen $2.50 lower, Brent 10-15 cents up.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen $2.50 lower, Brent 10-15 cents up.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures are expected to open lower on Monday, catching up with a sharp slide on world crude markets late Friday, dealers said.
Brent crude, meanwhile, is expected to open narrowly firmer, drawing breath after shedding 62 cents and plunging to its lowest level in London since April 10.
"The funds and chartists are hammering this market and the physical demand is not sufficient to hold it up," said a broker.
June gas oil should open $2-2.50 a tonne lower after settling at $164.25, while July Brent should come in 10-15 cents up on its Friday close of $17.70 a barrel, brokers said.

Brent took its cue on Friday from oil markets in the U.S., where prompt crude fell to its lowest level in 16 months as commodity funds baled out amid evidence of slack gasoline demand, rising crude inventories and record refinery production.
Renewal of the United Nations oil-for-food deal with Iraq, allowing Baghdad to sell another $2 billion worth of oil over the next six months, also gave speculators an excuse to sell.
But London brokers said the slide was overdone and Brent could expect to benefit from a degree of shortcovering.
"I certainly won't be advising anybody to sell it at these levels," said one.
Dealers saw key technical support around $17.48 a barrel, 11 cents below Friday's low and the lowest level for the prompt IPE crude contract since June 14, 1996.
"We might have to see a test of $17.50 before the market can make a decent recovery," said a broker.
